_what: The relation half of find_tools' corpus (dec:find-tools-also-finds-relations-and-points-to-what-joins-x-to-y, Anthony 2026-10-25): questions whose answer is a RELATION (a schema edge type), not a tool, phrased as a person asks them. A query passes when one of its accepted relations is among the `relations` find_tools returns (at most 3). `source` says where the words came from: `alex-grok-2026-10-10` is a query Alex's Grok chat sent to find_tools on flo2.io before it found INTERACTS_WITH through describe_schema (fact:root-cause-a-relation-with-no-typed-tool-cannot-be-found-by-find-tools-2026-10-25; four of its six are known, the other two are not recorded); `written-2026-10-25` was written by the agent that built this, which had read the schema's hints, so informed rather than blind. `known_misses` are the queries no word-matching can answer, each with the measured reason; the test holds that they still miss, so a pass is noticed and moved here.

known_misses.query: one thing is stopping another from going ahead
known_misses.why: No shared word: BLOCKS says "prevents or stalls", the person says "stopping" and "going ahead".

known_misses.query: these two records say the same thing twice
known_misses.why: No discriminating shared word: DUPLICATES says "cover the same ground", and "same" is common across the surface.

known_misses.query: the part of the system that offers this API
known_misses.why: No shared word: PROVIDES says "exposes/provides an Interface"; "part" pulls PART_OF_FLOW instead.

known_misses.query: draw a link from a person to the interface they operate
known_misses.why: "person" is nowhere in either relation's words, and "operate" is OPERATES_IN's name, which outranks both.

known_misses.query: connect a user role to the feature they use
known_misses.why: "user", "role" and "feature" are the Actor and Capability types' own words, not the relation's; counting an endpoint type's hint was measured and did not lift it.
